title: Investigation heuristic templates for KV prefetch and trace minimization
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working playbook and a small library of investigation templates focused on two recurring operator pain points we see in production inference: (1) KV cache prefetch/policy regressions that surface as cold-cache spikes and cost/latency anomalies and (2) trace bloat during high-volume incidents which makes root cause slow and expensive to debug. The intent is pragmatic: compact, copy-pasteable investigative lenses and dashboard widget snippets operators and SREs can use during oncall and postmortems.

Why now:
- Recent incidents (JIRA-OBS-1123, see linked ticket) showed rollout of a prefetch optimization that regressed tail latency for multi-turn chat paths.
- Trace storage and query cost increased ~18% in late Dec 2024 due to unbounded span replication in the new request fanout code.

Quick goals:
- Provide 3 investigation templates (prefetch heatmap, prefetch SLI decomposition, trace-minimization checklist).
- Propose 4 lightweight metric names and definitions for adoption by runtime and routing teams.
- Draft dashboard widget layouts minimizing cardinality while still actionable for oncall.

RULES OF THUMB used across templates:
- Prefer rate-based aggregations (per-minute counts) over raw counts to smooth burstiness.
- Keep tag cardinality low: tenant_id only for top-10 tenants, otherwise use tenant_bucket.
- Trace sampling: use severity-weighted sampling (100% for p99 latency incidents, 10% baseline).
- Don’t store full prompt content in spans; store prompt hash and a short prompt_type label only.

Metric definitions (suggested canonical names):
1) kv_prefetch_attempts_per_minute
   - type: gauge (rate)
   - description: number of prefetch calls invoked by runtime per minute (all models). Includes explicit prefetch triggered by routing policy and implicit warmers.
   - tags: model, shard, prefetch_policy

2) kv_prefetch_hit_rate_approx
   - type: ratio (0..1) computed as kv_prefetch_hits / kv_prefetch_attempts over sliding 5m window
   - description: approximate effectiveness of prefetch; does not include standard request-time cache hits.
   - tags: model, tenant_bucket

3) kv_eviction_tail_latency_ms
   - type: quantile metric (p50/p95/p99)
   - description: latency observed during eviction operations which indicates backend contention.
   - tags: shard, region

4) prefetched_prefix_waste_ratio
   - type: ratio (0..1)
   - description: fraction of prefetched prefixes never used by downstream token generation for the corresponding session (measure of wasted work). Computed daily per deployment.
   - tags: model_family, rollout_tag

Tracing conventions (span model):
- Span name: service.operation[.subtype] e.g., runtime.infer.kv-lookup or router.route.decision
- Span attributes to include (short keys only): model, shard, trace_role (operator|probe|user), cache_action (hit|miss|prefetch|evict), prompt_type
- Do NOT include: full raw prompt, full response, user ids (PII)
- Session correlation: use session_id and session_seq (keep session_seq integer) on root span only; downstream spans should reference session_id but not session payload.
- Sampling: severity-weighted policy (see below) with dynamic bump for detected high-latency routes

Sampling policy (templates):
- baseline: 5% trace sampling across runtime services for steady-state (minimizes cost)
- anomaly bump: if route_p95_latency > configured_threshold then raise sampling for that route to 100% for 10 minutes
- storage-protect: if trace budget > 85% of monthly quota, reduce baseline to 1% and increase anomaly bump threshold to reduce noise

Investigation template A: Prefetch heatmap (short checklist + query snippets)- Objective: quickly find which models/shards/tenants had prefetch failures or excessive waste during incident window.- Timebox: 15 minutes
Checklist:
  1) Confirm incident window and p99 latency spikes (source: main latency panel).
  2) Load prefetch attempts per minute by model and shard for window (5m rollup). Look for sudden drops in kv_prefetch_hit_rate_approx or spikes in kv_eviction_tail_latency_ms.
  3) Correlate with routing changes or rollout_tag (linked_artifacts might have PR ids).
  4) If prefetched_prefix_waste_ratio > 0.2 for a shard, mark as candidate for rollback.
SQL/TS query snippets (examples you can paste into Grafana/Influx):
  - SELECT model, shard, time_bucket('5m', ts) AS t, sum(kv_prefetch_attempts) FROM telemetry WHERE ts BETWEEN X AND Y GROUP BY model, shard, t ORDER BY t
  - SELECT shard, quantile(0.95) as p95 FROM kv_eviction_tail_latency_ms WHERE ts BETWEEN X AND Y GROUP BY shard
Interpretation heuristics:
  - High prefetch attempts + low hit_rate => over-eager prefetch policy or mis-specified prefix selectors
  - Low attempts + increased cold-start p99 => prefetch disabled or failing

Investigation template B: SLI decomposition for tail latency with minimal trace extraction- Objective: narrow the cause of p99 regressions to small set of subsystems without full trace replay.
Steps:
  1) Break down p99 by span-less metrics: network egress time, kv_eviction_tail_latency_ms, inference_compute_p99, router_decision_time_p99.
  2) If KV-related metrics explain >50% of extra p99, escalate to runtime team.
  3) If unexplained, activate targeted trace capture for 5% of requests on top 5 impacted tenants.
Mini-dashboard widgets to add:
  - p99 latency waterfall (stacked bars: router | kv-cache | compute | serialization)
  - top 10 shards by delta of kv_prefetch_hit_rate_approx vs baseline

Investigation template C: Trace-minimization checklist for postmortem storage cleanup- Objective: reduce trace volume and retain actionable data for future debugging while protecting cost.
Checklist:
  1) Remove duplicate spans in fanout: dedupe by (request_id, service.operation). If duplicates > 5% of spans, file infra PR.
  2) Convert high-cardinality span attributes (full prompt hash, tenant_id) to low-card buckets before storage.
  3) Apply TTL tiers: critical error traces -> 90d, normal incident traces -> 30d, baseline sampled traces -> 7d.
  4) Add hashing-based redaction for prompt snippets: store hash and prompt_type only.
  5) Add trace budget alerts to ops: monthly trace_quota_usage > 80% -> run automated compaction job.

Dashboard sketch notes (compact microdash approach):
- Goal: a single oncall pane that fits on a 1080p screen with 6 compact widgets. Avoid sprawling dashboards with 30+ panels.
- Widget 1 (Top-left): p99 latency small heatmap by model_family x shard (sparkline mini-heatmap).
- Widget 2 (Top-center): prefetched_prefix_waste_ratio sparkline + numeric delta vs baseline.
- Widget 3 (Top-right): kv_prefetch_hit_rate_approx numeric with sparkline and anomaly marker.
- Widget 4 (Bottom-left): small waterfall bar of quantile decomposition for selected route.
- Widget 5 (Bottom-center): trace budget gauge and current sampling rate.
- Widget 6 (Bottom-right): quick-links panel (flip to show recent rollouts, PRs, and a short checklist).
Design constraints for widgets:
- Use aggregated labels only (model_family, tenant_bucket); no free-form keys.
- Default time window = 30m for oncall, allow quick switch to 6h or 24h
- Hover telemetry should link to a trace quick-capture that pre-fills query parameters (route, shard, timestamp)

Operational runes (short action list for oncall):
- If prefetched_prefix_waste_ratio > 0.25 AND p99 increases by >15%: temporarily reduce prefetch aggressiveness to 'conservative' for affected shard(s) via routing flag.
- If kv_eviction_tail_latency_ms p99 > 200ms: shift traffic to sibling shard with warm cache and open paging investigation ticket.
- If trace_budget > 90%: reduce baseline sampling to 1% and prioritize anomaly-based sampling only.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should prefetched_prefix_waste_ratio be computed per-session or per-deployment? (cost vs signal fidelity tradeoff)
- What is canonical tenant bucketing policy for our dashboards? (top_10 + remainder vs percentile buckets)
- How should rollout_tag be attached to metrics to ensure backfills are feasible in long-term storage?

Short-term action items (owners assigned):
- Aisha: prototype 6-widget microdash in Grafana with the metric names above (target: 2025-01-22).
- Miguel: add kv_prefetch_attempts_per_minute and prefetched_prefix_waste_ratio to runtime telemetry (target: 2025-01-29).
- Jamie: implement severity-weighted sampling POC and open PR to telemetry repo (PR: link in linked_artifacts) (target: 2025-02-02).

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep the first iteration conservative: metrics that are cheap to compute and low-cardinality.
- Expect some noise: prefetch policies vary by model; aim to baseline per-model-family.
- When in doubt, prefer a short postmortem with actionable mitigation over capturing every bit of telemetry.

If you use this doc during an incident, please copy it into the incident ticket and annotate which template you followed. Add any new heuristics to the checklist and ping eng-observability for consolidation.
